title: Target Sum
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer target, determine the count of distinct expressions formed by adding '+' or '-' before each number in nums, such that the expression evaluates to the target.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer target, determine the count of distinct expressions formed by adding '+' or '-' before each number in nums, such that the expression evaluates to the target.
constraints: Assign exactly one plus or minus sign to EACH array position. Return the number of assignments whose signed sum equals target.
Equal values at different indices remain separate choices. +0 and -0 are different expressions, even though their numeric contributions agree.
hints: At each index there are two sign choices, including when the value is zero.
Cache the number of ways from an index to achieve a remaining signed sum.
Add ways(i+1,remaining-nums[i]) and ways(i+1,remaining+nums[i]); at the end count one only for remaining zero.
A suffix sum bounds the largest absolute contribution still possible. Memoization shares computation without merging distinct expression counts.
editorial: Recursive states track index and remaining target. The two outgoing branches count separate sign assignments even if they reach the same cached state. A suffix-sum bound safely prunes unreachable targets. With S=sum(nums), at most O(n*(S+1)) states are needed. The oracle independently enumerates every sign tuple and evaluates the resulting expression.

tests.explanation: Exactly one of the five positions receives a minus sign, so there are five different expressions.
Both +0+1 and -0+1 give 1. The zero doubles the number of expressions instead of disappearing.
